# Ergo: a brick-construction sandbox for agents

Project: https://github.com/ngrislain/ergo
Human guide: https://www.ergosandbox.com/#connect
Sandbox and REST origin: https://ergosandbox.com
Human authentication: https://ergosandbox.com/login#connect
Privacy: https://www.ergosandbox.com/privacy/
Terms: https://www.ergosandbox.com/terms/

## Authentication is a human-to-agent handoff

A human signs in with Google on the sandbox, chooses Generate access token,
and downloads ergo-mcp-token. Ask the human for the path to that private token
file, not their Google credentials, browser cookies, or cloud/S3 credentials.
There is no public remote MCP endpoint and no automatic device-code exchange.
The static information site does not issue, receive, or store agent tokens.

Tokens normally expire after one hour, never exceed 24 hours or the issuing
session's expiry, and are bound to https://ergosandbox.com. They authorize
permissioned shared-world reads, creation, assembly import and geometry commits.
They cannot change grants, retention, private snapshots, account plans, or mint
another delegation. Logging out does not individually revoke an issued token.

## Connect an MCP-capable agent

Build from source; a published npm release is not assumed:

git clone https://github.com/ngrislain/ergo.git
cd ergo
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.129 --locked
cargo xtask build-web
cargo build --release -p ergo-mcp

Configure a local stdio MCP process:
command: /absolute/path/ergo/target/release/ergo-mcp
args: --workspace /absolute/path/first-build.ergo.json
environment:
  ERGO_PUBLISH_URL=https://ergosandbox.com
  ERGO_PUBLISH_TOKEN_FILE=/absolute/path/ergo-mcp-token

The workspace parent directory must exist. A missing JSON file starts empty.
The bridge does not automatically load .env. A browser and the built WASM assets
are required. Local editing can operate without a hosted token; publication
requires one. Keep credentials out of tool arguments and URLs.

Equivalent start command, run from the cloned repository:

ERGO_PUBLISH_URL=https://ergosandbox.com \
ERGO_PUBLISH_TOKEN_FILE="$HOME/Downloads/ergo-mcp-token" \
./target/release/ergo-mcp --workspace "$HOME/first-build.ergo.json"

Change the token path to the actual downloaded file. The process waits for MCP
requests over stdio and opens the local browser runtime. Normally the MCP client
launches this process itself using the configuration above, one process per workspace.

## Start building

Discover the current tools and their JSON schemas. Start with get_catalog and
list_bricks. Use place_brick, move_brick, connect_bricks and grouping tools to
make a small grounded draft. Coordinates are X east, Y north, Z up.
Run validate_construction, test_stability_by_gravity, and
test_visual_appearance. Physical connector capacities need sourced measurements;
missing calibration must not be described as a successful calibrated validation.

publish_construction creates a new world/assembly or imports a new assembly into
an existing world. It does not update a previously published assembly in place.
MCP-created worlds allow signed-in collaborators by default; set
authenticated_editing=false for an owner/grant-only new world. Inspect confirmed
returned revisions and view_url. Do not automatically retry unknown or
accepted_unconfirmed publication outcomes: imports are not idempotent.

get_edit_allowance reports the current allowance. Free accounts have capacity
5,000 changed bricks, continuously refilling by 5,000 changes per 86400 seconds.
Authorization, operation budgets and physical validation remain authoritative.

## Direct REST access

Read GET /api/shared-worlds/allowance using Authorization: Bearer TOKEN.
Use that header for other shared-world endpoints. JSON writes also require
X-Ergo-Request: 1 and Content-Type: application/json.
POST /api/auth/mcp-token requires a human browser session, not a delegation.
